{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, removing commas
# First, check if any revenue values contain commas
print("Revenue values with commas:", df['revenue'].str.contains(',', regex=False).sum())

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Check for QA orders (should be 6, but found 0 in previous run)
qa_orders = df[df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]
print(f"Found {len(qa_orders)} QA orders with revenue 999999.99")

# Filter to completed orders only
completed_orders = df[df['status'] == 'completed']
print(f"Total completed orders: {len(completed_orders)}")

# Check for refunded orders
refunded_orders = df[df['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f"Total refunded orders: {len(refunded_orders)}")

# Check if any completed orders have revenue 999999.99
completed_qa = completed_orders[completed_orders['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]
print(f"Completed QA orders: {len(completed_qa)}")

# Now compute average revenue per completed order, excluding QA orders
df_filtered = completed_orders[completed_orders['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99]
mean_revenue = df_filtered['revenue_clean'].mean()
print(f"Average revenue per completed order (excluding QA): {mean_revenue:.2f}")

# Final report
df_filtered.head()"}
